newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo lifts gold profits, tougher 1997 looms.
newsitem.headline: Anglo lifts gold profits, tougher 1997 looms.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday its gold mines increased profits by nine percent in the quarter to end-December, helped by higher production and a higher gold price.
But the world's largest gold producer cautioned that its biggest mine would see production fall this year.
Available profit from the company's five gold mines amounted to 340.8 million rand ($73.6 million) in the three months to December 31.
Gold production rose three percent to 54 tonnes and the average gold price increased two percent to 55,756 rand per kg (2.2 lbs).
Available profit for the year to December 31 was up 158 percent to 1.27 billion rand.
Anglo said it expected gold production at Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd, the world's biggest gold mine, to fall 6.4 percent to 78 tonnes in 1997.
But other mines in its stable should produce more and the overall target for gold production in 1997 was 212.5 tonnes, one tonne less than in 1996.
The gold price has fallen below $350 an ounce for the first time in over three years.
Marketing director Kelvin Williams said he expected an eventual recovery in the gold price based on robust physical demand for the metal.
"There will be a turning (point) when gold will come back into favour," he said.
"We really see the gold market as being balanced on a robust gold offtake (and) satisfactory demand."
Williams said initial indications were that physical demand for gold in 1996 had matched the record levels seen in 1995.
